answer: Past the garden, every newcomer faces the same question — what does this identity actually cost? The entry fee is not fixed: it rises with the rate of new joins, so a sudden flood of identities makes each next one more expensive. The inlet rule turns a clone flood against itself — the first ten fakes are cheap, the thousandth costs a fortune, and the farm pays the surge it created. Hold the sparrow steady and the economy stays honest, because a clone army is only cheap when identities are free.
